atoms.text: When you have a choice, you can pick between different options or things. Picking one option or thing is called making a choice.

instruction.text: Frida is feeling quite annoyed today. She just can’t decide if she wants to go hiking or stay at home. Select Frida to help her make a choice.

feedback.end: First, Frida should think about some good reasons for going on a hike and some good reasons for staying at home.

instruction.text: Listen to Frida’s thoughts. Are they good reasons for going on a hike or for staying at home? Drag them to the correct groups.

hint.text: Frida can count how many good reasons she has for each option. Then, she can choose the option that has more reasons.

atoms.sound: If I went on a hike, I might be able to see all the way to the sea from the mountain top. That would be so cool!
I had to sit at my desk at work all week. I think fresh air and movement would do my body good.
The weather forecast says it might rain. I might as well stay at home.

feedback.finish: Now that she’s thought about it, there are more good reasons for going on a hike than for staying at home. But what about how she’s feeling?

instruction.text: Listen to Frida explaining how she feels. Knowing her feelings, should she go on a hike or not? Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Oh man, it has been a long week. Work was really exhausting, and I feel like I could use a relaxed afternoon sat on the sofa. That would be the perfect thing for my tired body.

feedback.finish: Counting reasons for and against something can be helpful, but feelings are also an important part of making a choice.

instruction.text: How should you make a choice? Select the correct answer.

b.sound: When you make a choice, try to think of reasons for, or against all the options. Then, think about your feelings too.
Just do what everyone else thinks you should do.
